Hi all — quick read-through from legal ops. A few notes for FinPlow to consider: 
- Subprocessor attestation: Redwood's standard clause requires 30 days notice for new subprocessors and an option to object. We provide a published registry and SOC2 reports for infra providers on request.
- Liability cap: Redwood's DPA mirrors our commercial agreement; if FinPlow needs higher limits for regulated processing, we can discuss via the commercial team (Karthik).
- Transfers: we maintain SCCs + supplementary measures. For customers wanting data residency guarantees, we can propose region-locked hosting under Dedicated/Private deployments.

Liam — if you can highlight the must-have changes vs nice-to-have in a single doc, that'll speed review. Also confirm whether you need a signed Subprocessor Attestation or certified SOC2 evidence for the listed providers.

- Execution: FinPlow prefers AdobeSign for our vendor platform (we have an AdobeSign connector to our vendor management system). Is Redwood able to sign via AdobeSign?
